solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swim poorly, swallowing tons — idiot!

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

indicators.note: something swallowing another takes it inside, so the word for ill encloses the letter for tons

parts.note: poorly is British for ill, sick

explanation.surface: Someone flounders in the water, gulping down huge amounts, and is mocked as a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is British slang for a stupid person, an insult like nitwit.

clue.text: A mutual easing of tensions inside ten terraced houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A calm settles among ten neighbours in a row of terraced homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is the diplomatic term, from French, for a relaxation of strained relations between states.

clue.text: Dash around island and cut up cruiser, maybe

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the string is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to dash is to race
C stands for circa, Latin for around
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone sprints round an island and slashes at something, perhaps a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RACE, C, I, LOP in this down entry; 'cruiser' suggests a ship but is US slang for a patrol car.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a cruiser is a police patrol car, so it is one example.

clue.text: Sports chiefs tucking into endless snacks and some sort of pudding

indicators.note: tucking into says the committee initials go inside the shortened snacks word
endless means the final letter of the snacks word is lost

parts.note: tapas are Spanish snacks
the IOC, International Olympic Committee, runs world sport

explanation.surface: Sporting bigwigs eating snacks and dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating but is the containment signal; 'endless' cuts the snacks word to TAPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca, made from cassava starch, is the basis of a classic milk pudding.

clue.text: Laugh when officer turns up, interrupting task

indicators.note: the turned letters interrupt, breaking into, the task word

parts.note: a chore is a task

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up says the officer abbreviation is written bottom to top

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Someone laughs when a senior officer arrives while they work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arrives, but in this down clue it writes the officer's letters as TL.
explanation.definitionFit: To chortle is to laugh gleefully, a word coined by Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Just impediment, see

parts.note: a bar is an obstacle or impediment
a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is one

explanation.surface: Read as a terse remark: an obstacle that is only just visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' here is the noun meaning a bishop's seat, not the verb; ELY is the cathedral city crosswords lean on most.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely and just are synonyms meaning only by a narrow margin, as in 'just made it'.

clue.text: First couple of builders chisel around power unit in plant

indicators.note: the first couple of builders means its opening two letters
around says the cheating word wraps around the power unit

parts.note: to chisel is slang for swindling, to cheat
kW, kilowatt, is a unit of power

explanation.surface: Builders chiselling around a power unit in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chisel' is the slang verb for swindle; 'plant' is botanical, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckwheat is a flowering crop grown for its grain-like seeds, a plant despite its name.

clue.text: Old belligerent Republican: last of the Washington crop

indicators.note: the last of the word the is its final letter

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, is Washington
oats are a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A warmongering Republican is the last of Washington's political crop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests US politics, but the answer is the British soldier the Americans fought in the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of past wars, combatants against the American colonists.

clue.text: Politicians invested in large universities with millions in one-off payment

indicators.note: invested in puts the politicians inside the large and universities letters

parts.note: U for university, doubled for the plural
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: MPs pour money into big universities as a single payout worth millions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is money paid all at once rather than in instalments.

clue.text: Relating to certain communications, push to abandon America amid rigged election

indicators.note: amid says the shortened push sits in the middle of the rearranged election
a rigged election is fixed or manipulated, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word election is the fodder for rearranging

indicators.note: the abbreviation for America abandons, or leaves, the word push, so those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: the word push as printed, before losing letters

explanation.surface: A political story: pressure on the US to walk away from a fixed vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' rearranges the fodder to TELEONIC, and 'amid' splits that after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Telephonic describes anything carried by telephone, one particular kind of communication link.

clue.text: Chuck and Mike gate-crashing party in NI

indicators.note: a gatecrasher forces their way in uninvited, so this letter goes inside the party's initials

parts.note: the DUP, Democratic Unionist Party, is a political party in Northern Ireland
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two men, Chuck and Mike, crash a party in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck looks like a man's name partnering Mike, but it is the verb meaning throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to throw it out, which is what 'chuck' means in informal speech.

clue.text: Audacity of the courts installing Democrat in district

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

indicators.note: the courting word installs, or houses, the letter for Democrat within it

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A complaint about judicial overreach: the boldness of courts putting a Democrat in charge of a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' is a verb here (woos), not the law courts the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Your neck of the woods is an idiom for the local area or neighbourhood you come from.

clue.text: Coppers heading off to arrest John in Vatican City, say

indicators.note: the shortened coins word holds the toilet word inside it, as an arrest holds a suspect
the opening letter, or head, of the coins word is cut off

parts.note: coppers are British copper coins, pennies, so pence
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav (lavatory)

explanation.surface: Police set off to seize a man called John inside the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers looks like police but means pennies; 'heading off' leaves ENCE, around LAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is an example of an enclave: a small state entirely surrounded by another country, here Italy.

clue.text: Food item's in middle of oven, within reach

indicators.note: the middle of oven is its central pair of letters

parts.note: something within reach is gettable, also spelt getable

explanation.surface: A dish sits in the oven, close enough to grab.
explanation.walkthrough: GETABLE is an accepted variant spelling of gettable.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable is an edible plant part, one type of food item.

clue.text: Unexpected debt I'm beginning to experience when retirement's due

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement signals that these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
I'm without its apostrophe gives these two letters

indicators.note: the beginning of experience means its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone facing a surprise debt just as they near retirement age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' turns DEBT into BEDT; retirement here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring can mean going to bed for the night, so bedtime is the hour that is due.

clue.text: Popular revolution protects rights over time: that's moral

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the preceding letters sit above the time letter

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the revolution word protects, or encloses, the rights letters

parts.note: a coup is a sudden overthrow, a revolution
R is the abbreviation for right, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A popular uprising guarding rights in the long run is ethically sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Incorrupt means not open to bribery or decay, an upright and ethical character.

clue.text: Get back into Soul Train

indicators.note: into says the turned word goes inside the word for soul

parts.note: the soul or heart of something is its core

indicators.note: back says the word get is read from right to left

parts.note: the word get as printed

explanation.surface: An instruction to return to watching the dance show Soul Train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GET into TEG, placed 'into' CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession, a long train of mourners following the coffin.

clue.text: End of rum — crew ultimately upset

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a crew is a body of men

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of upset

explanation.surface: The last of the rum is gone and the sailors are finally upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece or remnant, like an end of cloth.

clue.text: At sea, Walter Raleigh's first vessel

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the name is rearranged
first points to the opening letter of Raleigh's

explanation.surface: Sir Walter Raleigh's first ship out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges WALTER to TRAWLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trawler is a fishing boat that drags a net, one kind of vessel.

clue.text: Mostly offensive, he may be a member of the diplomatic corps

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the attack word is used

parts.note: an offensive is a military attack
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rude man who nonetheless might serve as a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims ATTACK to ATTAC; 'offensive' is a noun, not the adjective rude.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a specialist official attached to an embassy's staff, part of a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: Sportsman's father not taking sides, accepting foul shot

indicators.note: the trimmed word accepts, or takes in, the foul shot word
the sides are the outer letters, which are left off the word father

parts.note: the word father as printed
in tennis a let is a serve clipping the net, a faulty shot to be replayed

explanation.surface: A dad who stays neutral yet accepts a dirty shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking sides' leaves ATHE, and 'accepting' takes the tennis term inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a sportsman or sportswoman, particularly in track and field.

clue.text: Old-fashioned fuel was not good for cooking

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling or concocting, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fuel that proved poor for cooking with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges WAS, NOT and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Town gas was coal gas piped to homes before natural gas replaced it.

clue.text: Shunned by all after taking Friday off — this is ongoing

indicators.note: taking with off says the Friday letters are removed
off completes the instruction to take the Friday letters away

parts.note: someone shunned by everyone is friendless

explanation.surface: An outcast takes a Friday off from work, and it drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... off' removes FRI from FRIENDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means having no end, continuing without stop.

clue.text: What toddler does — briefly fidgeting when fast asleep

indicators.note: fidgeting is restless movement, so the gathered letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of does goes

parts.note: the word does as printed

explanation.surface: A toddler's restless squirming even when sound asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' clips DOES to DOE; 'fidgeting' then rearranges WHAT, TODDLER and DOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead to the world is an idiom for being so deeply asleep that nothing will wake you.

clue.text: Heard animal whimper

indicators.note: heard says the entry sounds like the word for the animal when spoken

parts.note: a mule is an animal, the offspring of a donkey and a horse

explanation.surface: An animal's soft whimper is overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to cry feebly, like a baby or kitten, much as one whimpers.

clue.text: Celestial body — object realigned, unseen — nothing odd in that

indicators.note: taking nothing odd from that string of words keeps only its even letters, the second, fourth, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: A star chart's object moved and lost from view, which is nothing strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing odd' means drop the odd letters of 'object realigned unseen', so B, E, T, E... remain; 'realigned' looks like an anagram signal but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Betelgeuse is a named star, a red supergiant in Orion, and stars are celestial bodies.

clue.text: Two ways to overcome resistance fast

indicators.note: the roads are placed over, around, the resistance symbol so it ends up inside them

parts.note: ST (street) and AVE (avenue) are two road abbreviations
R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: Advice on beating resistance quickly by having two routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is the verb meaning go without food, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, a severe form of fasting.

clue.text: Making a comeback, group is live with online content

indicators.note: making a comeback says the whole string comes back, read from its end

parts.note: a set is a group
taken as written
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A band reforms and plays live, streaming it online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a comeback' reads SET IS BE W from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Websites are collections of pages on the internet, the bulk of what people view online.
